standard_prerequisites.name: Numerical types, their Picard group, the bound on the weighted intersection numbers and the contraction step
standard_prerequisites.statement: A numerical type is a tuple of an integer and integer families of multiplicities, intersection numbers, weights and genera subject to the five defining conditions of the chapter, and its Picard group is the cokernel of the matrix of divided intersection numbers; the genus of the type is the alternating sum determined by those data, and the topological genus is the expression in terms of the number of vertices and the positive intersection pairs. The chapter bounds the weighted intersection numbers of a minimal type of genus at least two, proves that a type of nonpositive genus has Picard group the integers, that a minimal type has genus at least the topological genus and that the torsion of a Picard group can be read off through the divided intersection matrix. The author's own definitions and lemmas of the chapter are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proposition is the arithmetic estimate that makes the classification of the minimal types of a fixed genus finite, and it is the last ingredient of that classification in this section.

core_obligations: Reduce to a bounded numerical type: by the chapter's estimate the weighted intersection numbers of a minimal type of genus at least two are bounded in terms of the genus, so the type lies in a finite set and it suffices to bound the torsion for the types in that set (source lines 4301-4308).

Apply the contraction machinery: the comparison of the Picard groups of a type and of a contracted type, together with the description of the genus of a contracted type, shows that the torsion can only grow in a controlled way under contractions, so one may assume the type minimal (source lines 4308-4314).

Use the two structural lemmas: the genus of a minimal type dominates the topological genus, and the torsion of the Picard group is computed by the divided intersection matrix, which together with the first step bounds the dimension of the torsion in terms of the genus (source lines 4314-4318).

Conclude the estimate: the dimension of the torsion subspace over the field with the given number of elements is at most the genus, which is the assertion for every prime exceeding the bound (source lines 4318-4319).

proof_roadmap.step: Bound the type using the weighted-intersection estimate and reduce to a finite set of shapes.
Reduce to a minimal type via the contraction comparison of Picard groups.
Bound the torsion through the genus comparison and the divided intersection matrix.
Read off the dimension bound over the finite field.
